articles.title: Weapons stolen from Ukraine front line handed to notorious neo-Nazi unit
articles.body:
Weapons stolen from Ukraine front line handed to notorious neo-Nazi unit
Ukraine’s State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) has announced the transfer of weapons worth about $100,000 confiscated from an alleged smuggling ring to the notorious Azov Corps.
The cache, including about 17,000 rounds of ammunition, grenades, single-shot anti-tank grenade launchers, land mines and other weapons, according to the Ukrainian agency, was handed over this week, having been seized in May.
A criminal group had used a humanitarian vehicle to transport the weapons stolen from the front line to Ivano-Frankivsk Region in Western Ukraine, the DBR has alleged.
The weapons were intended for sale on the black market, but will instead be used by Azov, the agency said, describing its members as “defenders of Ukraine.”
Azov originated as an ultranationalist Ukrainian volunteer militia amid the country’s bloody armed coup in 2014, before being incorporated into the country’s security forces. The unit has been widely accused of atrocities and war crimes by both Russia, which designated it a terrorist organization in 2022, and Western organizations, including the UN, Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International.
Prior to the escalation of the conflict with Russia in 2022, US lawmakers had sought to restrict military assistance to the unit, citing its members’ far-right ideology. Western governments have since expanded their cooperation with the formation.
Moscow has for years warned that the Ukraine conflict would become a major source of illicit weapons for criminal groups and has alleged that elements within the Ukrainian state could be protecting trafficking networks.
Law enforcement agencies in several European countries have also warned about the risk that weapons from Ukraine could enter criminal markets.
Ukrainian organized crime tends to become joined at the hip with corrupt officials, as showcased earlier this month by the exposure of a protection racket operating in the prosecutor general’s office, which collected fees from scam-call centers.
The accusations by Western-backed anti-graft investigators forced the resignation of Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko. The former key ally of Vladimir Zelensky has fled the country and reportedly resides in Vienna now.

articles.title: Russia launches terrorism-related case against London councilor
articles.body:
Russia launches terrorism-related case against London councilor
The Russian authorities have announced a terrorism-related criminal case against a Russian-British woman who serves as a councilor in the London borough of Ealing.
Moscow has accused Ksenia Maximova of lobbying the British government to advance an anti-Russian government agenda, potentially in coordination with British Intelligence services and collaborating with a London law firm run by Ukrainian-British citizens allegedly on behalf of Kiev.
Maximova is associated with the Russian Anti-War Committee, backed by exiled oligarch Mikhail Khodorkovsky, and is an active participant in a network of groups based in the West that seeks to overthrow the Russian government and fracture the country by promoting Western military support for Ukraine, among other things.
Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) announced on Monday that it opened a criminal case against her over alleged participation in an organization designated as ‘terrorist’ under Russian law.
As director of the Russian Democratic Society UK (RDS), which was designated as an ‘undesirable organization’ in Russia earlier this month, Maximova has overseen stunts by Russian emigres and artists protesting in support of Ukraine in front of the Russian Embassy in London.
She is also ‘consul’ for the Russian Anti-War Committee, which was declared a ‘terrorist organization’ by the Russian Supreme Court in March.
The RDS presents itself as “an alternative Russia,” and has lobbied for additional sanctions, including measures targeting Russia’s oil trade, the FSB said.
London has for decades harbored rich individuals who acquired their wealth abroad under shady circumstances, including Russian businessmen who amassed fortunes during the privatizations that followed the collapse of the Soviet Union.
Former oligarchs, including Khodorkovsky, have used their resources and connections to support Russian opposition groups and undermine the Russian government.

articles.title: UK police arrest five men amid bomb alert outside US air base
articles.body:
UK police arrest five men amid bomb alert outside US air base
The UK authorities have apprehended five men on suspicion of plotting a terrorist attack outside RAF Fairford, an air base that also hosts US warplanes involved in strikes against Iran.
According to a statement by Gloucestershire Police Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone on Sunday, police received “a call relating to three suspicious vehicles travelling towards RAF Fairford.” Local media later described the vehicles as three white vans.
Officers arriving at the scene subsequently arrested five individuals near the village of Whelford “on suspicion of committing offenses under the Explosives Act,” with Counter Terror Police investigating what officials called a “major incident.”
The BBC published an unverified photo purportedly showing the arrested suspects sitting half-naked on the ground with their hands behind their backs and faces blurred.
A British Army bomb disposal unit was sent to examine the vehicles, and around 85 households were evacuated as a precaution, Ocone told reporters. UK media outlets have shown what appears to be helicopter footage depicting a specialized wheeled robot operating near the vans.
Local residents who have nowhere else to stay have been provided temporary shelter inside a leisure center.
Commenting on the incident in a post on X, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged “people not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts.”
Later on Sunday, Gloucestershire Constabulary’s temporary chief constable, Maggie Blyth, gave an update, saying the authorities believe the “matter to be contained.” She declined to reveal whether the police are looking for more suspects.
She added that local residents would not be able to return to their homes tonight.
Sky News reported that while there are so far no conclusions, police are looking into potential Iranian involvement in the suspected bomb plot, among several other lines of inquiry; Reuters published a similar report.
The US Air Force has operated out of RAF Fairford for decades, with heavy bombers stationed at the base, including bombers used in strikes against Iran.
In July, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps issued a statement warning the UK specifically that “any base used to launch attacks on Iranian territory is a legitimate target for our forces.”
Commenting on the incident, a US military spokesperson told local media that the Pentagon is “working closely with our UK counterparts to monitor this situation.”
US President Donald Trump told reporters that the suspects “were looking to do big damage to our fort.”
“We had them under investigation… We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” he said.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: Ukraine strikes 2 defense plants in Russia, oil facilities
articles.body:
The Defense Forces of Ukraine have launched strikes on two defense plants in Russia's Tula and Voronezh regions, as well as oil facilities in the Krasnodar Krai, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has reported.
"This night, our sanctions were applied against two defense plants – in the Tula and Voronezh regions. SBU units worked well over the past 24 hours on the aggressor's oil facilities in the Krasnodar region," Zelenskyy wrote in a Telegram post on Monday.
According to him, targets in Kaluga and Oryol regions, which Russia uses for drone attacks against Ukraine, were also hit, while operations were carried out against the Russian occupation contingent in the Bryansk region.
Zelenskyy also reported a hit on a target in the Black Sea.
Subsequently, the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) reported on its Telegram channel about successful strikes carried out overnight Monday on four oil depots in Russia's Krasnodar Krai.
"Drones of the SBU's Alpha Special Operations Center hit the Edelweiss-95 and Din-Yug-Oil oil depots in the stanitsa of Novotitarovskaya. Two separate fire centers were recorded there. A strike was also delivered against the Lukoil-Yugnefteprodukt oil depot in the stanitsa of Pavlovskaya. A fire is raging at the facility," the Ukrainian special service said.
According to the agency, another successful hit was registered at the Angelinskaya oil depot in the stanitsa of Staronizhestebliyevskaya, where a fire is also ongoing.
"These are important elements of the fuel infrastructure that ensure the storage and supply of petroleum products for the Russian army," the SBU emphasizes.

articles.title: Threat of Russian sabotage in Europe has grown, says Finnish intelligence official
articles.body:
The threat of Russian sabotage in Europe has increased over the summer.
Teemu Liikkanen, head of counterintelligence at the Finnish Security and Intelligence Service (Supo), says the threat is real in Finland too, although there is no indication of any immediate danger.
"There is no reason to panic or become fearful. We should not go down that road. But we need to be prepared and ready," Liikkanen said on Yle's breakfast show on Monday.
In Finland, the targets most vulnerable to Russian sabotage are particularly the defence industry and activities supporting Ukraine.
Russia has carried out sabotage in countries supporting Ukraine for several years. Sabotage activity was noticeably quieter in 2025, but the threat has now increased again.
Jyrki Isokangas, a retired colonel and university lecturer at the University of Jyväskylä, said Russia is seeking to drive a wedge between Western countries and undermine support for Ukraine.
"Russia is trying to create an atmosphere in Western countries in which helping Ukraine is seen as something that you shouldn't or can't do," he added.
Isokangas does not, however, believe Russia wants to challenge Nato through military action.
Russia is believed to have been behind the arson attack on a Starlink satellite station in Poland last week.
President Alexander Stubb has meanwhile urged Finns to prepare themselves mentally for possible acts of sabotage.

articles.title: Russian drone strikes on Kiev kill three as Zelenskyy decries 'Shahed terror'
articles.body:
Russian drone strikes targeting the Ukrainian capital Kiev have killed at least three people and wounded more than 10 others, regional authorities announced, as Moscow launched a widespread aerial offensive across the country.
A strike hit a local market in the village of Sofiivska Borshchahivka, according to the Kiev regional prosecutor's office, whilst other drone impacts damaged civilian vehicles and ignited major fires across commercial warehouses and office buildings in the capital region.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed that Russian forces launched 277 attack drones of various models since Saturday, inflicting damage on civilian infrastructure nationwide, including a facility utilised as the official residence of the Saudi Arabian ambassador.
De-escalation doubts
In a statement posted on X, Zelenskyy said the drone wave across Kiev destroyed kindergartens, schools, residential homes, an auto repair facility, and communications infrastructure.
Additional strikes struck a sports school in Dnipro and a children's home in the Sumy region.
"Russia has no military objective whatsoever in doing this – it is purely an attempt to break people and inflict as much harm as possible on our society," Zelenskyy said.
He dismissed Moscow's recent diplomatic overtures, arguing they are designed solely to forestall decisive international measures: "If Russia were truly preparing for any real steps toward de-escalation – as it claims, particularly to American negotiators – this wave of 'shahed' terror would not be happening."
The Russian Defence Ministry said via Telegram that its forces struck communications and logistics hubs alongside a cargo vessel allegedly ferrying military supplies in Kiev and Odesa, reiterating its stance that it targets only military assets.
